content.title: No. 18 Purdue engineers upset in Big Ten final, denies No. 3 Michigan back-to-back conference tourney titles
content.text: CHICAGO — Braden Smith flexed to the Purdue bench before beating his chest. He’s a selfless point guard, so much so that he’s now one dime away from tying Bobby Hurley for the most career assists in NCAA Division I history. But this was the senior’s moment in his final Big Ten tournament game.Smith had just muscled a shot over 7-foot-3 Michigan center Aday Mara, the Big Ten Defensive Player of the Year. The 6-foot playmaking Smith drew the foul and watched as the ball danced around the rim and fell through the net.AdvertisementThe Boilermakers were up double digits, chugging along midway through the second half, the United Center sounded like Purdue’s Mackey Arena, and Michigan head coach Dusty May had to call a timeout to try to recalibrate a Wolverines team that was gunning for back-to-back Big Ten tournament titles.Yet the Wolverines couldn’t climb out of the hole they dug, falling 80-72 on Sunday. No. 18 Purdue (27-8, 13-7 Big Ten), the AP’s preseason No. 1 but ultimately just the seventh seed in the Big Ten, won its fourth game in four days, seized the conference tournament crown for the third time in program history and dethroned No. 3 Michigan (31-3, 19-1), which won a league-record 19 games in the regular season.The victory allowed the Boilermakers to jump from a No. 3 seed in the NCAA tournament into a No. 2 spot. They’ll face No. 15 Queens in the West Region in St. Louis on Friday.Smith finished with 14 points, 11 assists and 0 turnovers. Forward Trey Kaufman-Renn stacked 20 points on 10-of-15 shooting. The Wolverines were paced by Big Ten Player of the Year Yaxel Lendeborg, who finished with 20 points and four 3s.Purdue responded to a game-opening 3 from Michigan's Nimari Burnett with seven straight points. That run featured a shot fake and make by the Boilermakers' all-time leading 3-point marksman, Fletcher Loyer, and culminated in a two-handed flush from Australian big man Oscar Cluff. Loyer clocked out with 14 points, and Cluff had 21.AdvertisementMichigan quickly bounced back, in part thanks to two additional triples: one more from Burnett, and then Lendeborg, a day removed from his last-second game-winner against Wisconsin in the tournament's semifinals, splashed another.Smith supplied helpers on two of the Boilermakers' first four field goals. Initially, he continued to struggle to relocate his jump shot. He went a combined 4 of 23 from the field in the previous three Big Ten tournament games, and he started Sunday's final 0 of 3.Smith eventually ended his scoring drought with 8:47 to go in the first half after a wardrobe change.“I think when I ripped my jersey and switched to 41, I think that helped,” Smith said postgame somewhat jokingly.Braden Smith ripped his No. 3 jersey vs. Michigan and had to put on a No. 41 jersey for the rest of the Big Ten Tournament final 😳 😅 pic.twitter.com/KxYxMEdqiE— Yahoo Sports (@YahooSports) March 15, 2026He later added: “I ripped it, fully with both hands like Superman style. I was really frustrated. Just a lot of misses these past four games, and I was just frustrated because I put a lot of time and work in. Obviously when you don’t see the results, it kind of gets to you, and it got to me at that point.”AdvertisementThe results came when he was wearing No. 41. There was no name on the back of the jersey, but his handles were still recognizable. Smith yo-yoed the ball on a crossover that set up a silky smooth midrange jumper to tie the game 17-17.Unfortunately for Purdue, its two key frontcourt players, Kaufman-Renn and Cluff, both had two fouls less than 12 minutes in.Lendeborg also picked up two first-half personals, including one on a Loyer 3-point attempt that the senior guard transformed into a 4-point play, which trumped a step-back 3 Elliot Cadeau sank moments earlier. Cadeau also served up an alley-oop for Aday Mara.AdvertisementMara was soon on the other end of a lob, dialing up a perfectly placed pass for a flying Lendeborg.Michigan and Purdue were trading blows before the Boilermakers made a move. They did so with Cluff saddled on the bench with three fouls. Matt Painter’s team orchestrated a 9-0 surge that saw redshirt freshman guard Jack Benter drill a 3-pointer. A couple tough makes inside from Cadeau helped Michigan knot things up 38-38 by intermission, though.Purdue outscored Michigan 22-8 to start the second half. That’s largely because of the two-man game between Smith and Kaufman-Renn.Smith penetrated, found Kaufman-Renn and watched the forward go to work. Rinse and repeat. Smith called his own number, too, like for the and-1 that forced May to call time. Together, they scored 17 of the Boilermakers’ first 24 second-half points.AdvertisementAfter trailing by as many as 14 points, Michigan did its best to counter. A pair of dunks from Mara rejuvenated the maize and blue faithful.And a 3 from Lendeborg pulled the Wolverines within five, 68-63, with 3:47 left. That’s as close as their comeback bid got them, however. Cluff dropped in a hook shot and Loyer made a pair of free throws after being fouled from beyond the arc again.Fittingly, Smith helped the Boilermakers seal their second Big Ten tournament championship since he got to campus ahead of the 2022-23 season, as he blocked a Cadeau 3-point attempt down the stretch. Cluff put the exclamation point on the triumphant win with a thundering slam after Purdue broke Michigan’s press.AdvertisementBut, again, Sunday was Smith’s moment. He starred for a Purdue team he’s given everything the past four seasons, including two Big Ten tournament titles that bookend a prolific college career.Live coverage is over175 updatesSun, March 15, 2026 at 6:25 PM UTCYahoo Sports StaffSun, March 15, 2026 at 9:37 PM UTCYahoo Sports StaffMichigan is still projected to land the 1 seed in the Midwest region, while Purdue likely secured its spot as a No. 2 seed with today’s win.
